newsitem.title: CANADA: NOVA, TCPL set one-stop gas service.
newsitem.headline: NOVA, TCPL set one-stop gas service.

text.p: Canadian pipeline firms NOVA Corp and TransCanada PipeLines Ltd, under pressure from competing pipeline proposals, said on Tuesday they would offer natural gas shippers one-stop access to both systems.
The companies said they expected to implement the plan, which has been likened to code-sharing in the airline industry, after consulting with customers in their markets.

NOVA unit NOVA Gas Transmission Ltd operates Alberta's 12 billion cubic feet per day natural gas pipeline network, one of North America's biggest. TransCanada's seven BCF mainline stretches across Canada to Quebec from Alberta.
The companies said the one-stop service would streamline customer contracting, gas flow management and billing.
"This is a major change that further enhances Alberta's competitive natural gas advantage," said Eric Shelton, NOVA Gas Transmission's vice-president of transportation marketing.

NOVA and TCPL, which face competing, producer-backed proposals from Alliance Pipeline and Palliser Pipeline, said their new seamless service, which requires regulatory approval, would offer several benefits to current and future customers.
Under the arrangement, a single point of contact would be set for both systems, eliminating the need for dealing with both companies.
Also, customers would process only one invoice for combined transportation on both systems.
The move is similar to code-share agreements in the airline industry, which allow companies to place their own flight codes and sell seats on partners' aircraft without extra billing.
The firms said plans include use of NrG Highway, the information system used for electronic commerce on interconnecting pipeline systems. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
